en.title: Titles and forms of address
en.summary: How to address people in speech and in writing.

paragraphs: The right form of address shows respect. Here is a short guide, in a note from a school secretary.

Dear parents, please address the teachers as Mr Green, Ms Hall or Dr Patel. Do not use the first name unless the teacher asks you to. In an e-mail, begin with Dear Mr Green and end with Yours sincerely. Thank you.

**1. A title goes with a surname.** Say Mr Green or Dr Patel, never Mr John. In British writing the full stop is usually left out: Mr, Mrs, Dr. In American writing it is kept: Mr., Mrs., Dr. See Introduction to Grammar: Personal pronouns and address.

paragraphs: **2. Formal letters have a fixed pattern.** Begin with Dear and a title with the surname. End with Yours sincerely when you know the name, and Yours faithfully when you do not. See Introduction to Grammar: Word formation and register.

items: **Ms** is a safe choice: it does not show whether a woman is married. **Mrs** is for married women and **Miss** for unmarried women.
**Sir** and **madam** are used in shops, hotels and restaurants.
In American e-mail, **Hi Mr Green** is not usual; use **Dear Mr Green** in formal messages.

paragraphs: Many workplaces use first names quickly, even with managers. If you are not sure, begin with the title and wait to be invited to use the first name.
